subject: Post-demo: Polaris trial scope, differentiation vs hyperscalers, test milestones
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@polarishealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed test plan and asks

Asha — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a suggested next-steps cadence so we can turn the demo momentum into a short, focused evaluation.

What we heard from Polaris
- Primary objective: reduce inference cost while keeping 95th p99 latency under 200ms for your triage prompts.
- Data residency and key management are gating items (HIPAA-adjacent).
- You want a short, results-oriented bake-off vs the hyperscaler endpoints you currently run for anonymized triage traffic.

How Redwood wants to structure the trial (proposal) — 3 short tests, 10 business days total
1) Microbench latency test (1–2 days): steady-state p50/p95/p99 on your standard prompt shapes; include cold-start and warmed-KV runs. Owner: Redwood eng (Rishi).
2) E2E user prompt set (5 days): run your anonymized production prompt set (attached sample) and compare throughput, cost-per-prompt, and qualitative output parity on a small evaluation subset. Owner: Polaris / SRE + Redwood eng.
3) Failure and fallback exercise (2–3 days): simulate partial capacity, region failover, and a model-fallback path to ensure graceful degradation. Owner: Redwood infra + Polaris SRE.

Success criteria (examples — we can refine):
- Cost: <= 0.6x of hyperscaler baseline on average cost-per-token (or agreed threshold).
- Latency: p99 <= 200ms for warmed KV in our dedicated config.
- Quality: no more than 4% regression in your eval pass-rate on the golden prompt set.

Immediate asks from Polaris (so we can schedule):
- Confirm a 5-day window in July for the E2E run and provide an anonymized sample of 10k prompts (we included a 200-example CSV as a format example).
- Confirm whether KMS/HSM integration is required for this evaluation (we support ephemeral keys for the trial).
- Polaris SRE contact and availability for a 30–45 minute kick-off to provision access.

Please reply with availability for the kick-off (we're proposing Tue/Wed next week) and any non-starters on the proposed success criteria. Once we lock that, Rishi will share the runbook and infra steps.

Thanks — excited to get this scoped and started.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: polaris-workload-sample.csv (csv, 32KB), redwood-bakeoff-checklist.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: Asha Rao <asha@polarishealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Polaris SRE <sre@polarishealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed test plan and asks

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan and the sample. A few clarifications from our team before we lock dates: 

1) KMS/HSM: we will need to use our KMS for any keys used in live data pipelines. For the trial, we can accept ephemeral keys if that keeps onboarding fast, but production will require our KMS.
2) Dataset: we'll provide a 10k anonymized prompt set but need guidance on the anonymization checklist (PII strips, tokenization notes). Can you confirm Redwood's recommended process?
3) Hyperscaler baseline: we currently run inference on XCloud's managed LLM endpoints and will share the baseline token-cost and a CSV of p50/p95/p99 latencies for our top prompt classes.

Availability: Polaris SRE can do a kick-off Wed 7/7 at 11:00am PT or Thu 7/8 at 2:00pm PT. Which works for your team?

—
Asha Rao
Head of AI Platforms | Polaris Health
asha@polarishealth.ai

P.S. please send your anonymization checklist and we'll prepare the sample accordingly.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@polarishealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Polaris SRE <sre@polarishealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed test plan and asks

Asha — Wed 7/7 11:00am PT works for us. Confirming a 30–45 minute kick-off.

Quick answers to your questions and internal owners copied: 
- KMS/HSM: for the evaluation we typically use ephemeral keys and keep data in an anonymized sandbox. We can walk through KMS integration during the canary days; Rishi, please flag the short list of steps for Polaris KMS onboarding.
- Anonymization checklist: attached — short checklist (PII remove, hash user ids, normalize timestamps). If you can send the 10k set in that format we will prioritize the E2E run.
- Baseline inputs: appreciate sharing the XCloud baseline; we will align measurement windows and compare apples-to-apples (same prompt ordering, same tokenization).

Internal note / action items for Redwood (short) — team, please treat this as a 10-business-day sprint once we start:
- Rishi: own runbook + infra; create dedicated test cluster and provide an access checklist for Polaris SRE.
- Karthik: coordinate commercial guardrails — what pricing model do we run for the trial and what protections do we expose for cost spikes?
- Ben: I'll loop you in for the procurement/contract redline if Polaris requests a short-term trial SOW.

Karthik / Rishi — can you both confirm owners and estimated ETA to have a runbook + infra ready post-kickoff? I'll schedule the kickoff for Wed 7/7 11am PT and share a calendar invite.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: redwood-anonymization-checklist.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Polaris trial commercial & owners

Marissa — confirmed. I can own the pricing guardrails for the trial. Proposed commercial approach: 
- Trial pricing: time-bound flat rate for the 10-business-day evaluation capped at an agreed token budget. This avoids surprise overages and lets Polaris compare unit economics.
- Optional: enable a burst override with pre-approval for emergency runs (logged and billed).

Estimated ETA: I will draft a short SOW + pricing attachment within 48 hours of kickoff. Ben, please standby in case Polaris asks for a procurement-level SOW.

I'll also prepare a short billing FAQ we can share with Polaris during the kickoff.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Marissa / team — I will prepare the runbook and a bare-metal test cluster template. Timeline:
- Draft runbook (infra steps, KMS notes, dataset ingest): by EOD Mon 7/6.
- Cluster ready for Polaris access (ephemeral keys + warmed cache path): by Thu 7/9 morning PT.

I've uploaded the initial runbook and test-plan checklist here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-runbook-pol-2026 — Polaris SRE, please confirm you can access, and I'll add an infra access checklist to the doc.

I will also include a short script to reproduce the hyperscaler baseline tokenization so our comparisons are aligned.
